objective: Building a basic FMEA and calculating and interpreting risk priority numbers
secondaryObjectives: Applying lean concepts: flow, takt time, just-in-time, the theory of constraints and going to the gemba

sources.cite: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 6.3.2.1 Shewhart X-bar and R and S Control Charts
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: X-bar chart UCL = x-double-bar + A2 R-bar, center line x-double-bar, LCL = x-double-bar - A2 R-bar; R chart UCL = R-bar D4, center line R-bar, LCL = R-bar D3; A2 = 3/(d2 sqrt(n)). The factor values used (A2 = 0.577, D3 = 0, D4 = 2.114 for subgroups of 5) are the standard table values and were not on the fetched page; the limits in the case (R-bar 3.1 g: 500.2 to 503.8 g, R up to 6.55 g) are computed from them. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's cssgb-fill-weight-chart (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You lead improvement on the dispatch line of a fictional online retailer's warehouse. Orders must ship the same day; 480 orders arrive in an 8-hour shift.
handover: The packing station takes 1.2 minutes per order; labelling takes 0.9.
howItWorks: The console shows the open dataset, its quality flags and a table of the checks and their results.
Move on a day at a time. A decision comes to you at each tollgate; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Day 2: overtime runs every evening; costs rise 15% and same-day shipping still slips on busy days.
Day 3: wrong labels keep shipping parcels to the wrong customers; mis-shipment costs don't fall.
Day 4: the manual check slows packing below takt; same-day shipping fails for a week.

choices.label: Takt time is 480 / 480 = 1.0 minute per order; packing at 1.2 is the constraint, so balance packing (a second packer at peak)
choices.feedback: Takt time is available time divided by demand; a step slower than takt is the constraint.

choices.label: Speed up labelling
choices.feedback: Labelling is already under takt; the constraint is packing.

choices.label: Add overtime every day
choices.feedback: It hides the constraint at a cost.

choices.label: RPNs: wrong label 8 x 6 x 7 = 336, late pickup 7 x 3 x 2 = 42, damaged pack 5 x 4 x 3 = 60; act on wrong labels first, and note its high severity
choices.feedback: RPN = severity x occurrence x detection; the highest, with high severity, comes first.

choices.label: Rank by severity only
choices.feedback: Ignores how often and how detectably it happens.

choices.label: Fix late pickups: the courier complains most
choices.feedback: Late pickup's RPN is 42; wrong labels are 336.

actPrompt.title: Reducing the wrong-label RPN
actPrompt.context: Detection is poor: nobody checks labels.

choices.label: Add a scan-to-verify step (poka-yoke) matching label to order before sealing, then re-score: detection 2, RPN 96

effects.log: Scan-to-verify is added; RPN falls to 96.

choices.feedback: Mistake-proofing improves detection or prevents occurrence; re-scoring shows the effect.

choices.label: Retrain packers to be careful
choices.feedback: Helps occurrence a little; detection unchanged.

choices.label: Add a final manual inspection of every parcel
choices.feedback: Slows the constraint further and misses errors when tired.

scoring.modelReasoning: Takt time is available time divided by customer demand; a step slower than takt is the constraint to balance. A process FMEA scores each failure mode's severity, occurrence and detection; RPN = S x O x D sets priority (high severity counts on its own). Actions that mistake-proof (poka-yoke) cut occurrence or improve detection; re-score to confirm.
